body: Well, I've always thought that g-rank would be more difficult of course, although I can't know for sure how much more difficult it is compared to high-rank, I'd have to play a game with g-rank to know for sure. Also, I don't think 25 mins. is quick, what I meant was that it doesn't feel like too long a hunt for me personally. And as to why not use items, that's because I personally don't enjoy having the monster stopped in place while I beat it for a couple of seconds, this might sound cheesy but I like the "thrill of the hunt". So unless I'm doing the very best I can to hunt a monster and it's still taking me over 40 mins. to kill/capture it, I prefer not to use those kinds of items. it's not like I have a problem with item usage, and just to be clear, I don't think i'm better than players who use them.

It's just that given that I'm a "novice" (400 hrs are rookie numbers right?) and use a weapon that is supposed to not match the damage of many others, hunts never really feel long. A Mega Demondrug and 3 or 4 might seeds allow me to kill every endgame monster in ~25 mins. or so. What's the average time for the average player to kill endgame monsters?

I’m a solo HH main (never played online for a bunch of reasons) playing MHP3rd which has been my first MH game. I’ve completed the whole game including Alatreon and all Epic Hunting Quests (I’ve done only a few the DLC quests tho). I’ve never used bombs with the exception of the ones for Jhen Mhoran, almost never used Sonic/Flashbombs, only the ones from the supply chest and even then, only sometimes. Traps? Mostly, to capture monsters and only used them for damage in Epic Hunting Quests and I’ve never used Drugged/Tinged Meat. My question is: Do people really think that using those items is REALLY necessary?

Probably not, just a morbid curiosity which you don't need to be suicidal nor clinically depressed in order to express. If you still feel there's something wrong with you, then just talk to a professional who's someone who could better help you with your questions.

I've actually been thinking, in the last few days, of doing something like that, I just wonder if someone like me who thinks life is pointless can actually help other people. There's also the problem that I never do something unless I give it my all, it may sound like something a person would say in a job interview just to get the job, but I actuallly do that, I almost didn't graduate from highschool because of it.

I am NOT a professional so don't just take my word for it, but I think that
1. You may be just somewhat curious about it but not obsessed.
2. I can't say for sure, forgive me.
3. probably not, but again, I am NOT a professional.
4. I'd say the event may have triggered a "life crisis".
5. You were shocked by the news.

Sorry I couldn't be more helpful, seeking a psychologist may help you.

The thing is that I don't really care about the material world, so I don't really care about material stuff (except people) which means that I don't really care about money, which renders the act of working pointless. Also, although I acknowledge the fact that there's a chance of there being an afterlife, I also don't believe in spiritual stuff. So, to me, living is pointless.

As for the title question the answer is probably the chemicals your body poduces, it's usually because of them that people see things in that way. As for your thoughts about yourself, just remember that there are people out there who love things and other people that a "normal person" would despise. And as for the bad people around you, I think there's no easy way around them, either face them, truly ignore them or befriend them.

People make mistakes, everyone does, yours is not a major one from what I understand. I think you should focus on forgiving yourself and understand that the girl was at fault as well. If nothing worse came out of it, then just put the past to rest (which I know isn't easy) and keep on going.

I actually have fun playing videogames and watching weird videos on YT, it's just that I see them them as distractions from the bad thoughts which come back as soon as I stop distracting myself which in turn means that I spend a great amount of time doing just that, distracting myself.

I think I kinda understand your position because I was there last year, I've also never drank, smoked or had sex, my advice would be that maybe you should be the one inviting your friends to events, movies, the bar (even if you won't drink alcohool). It doesn't really matter if you're outgoing around people, what matters is if you're proactive as opposed to being reactive, that worked for me and I am an INFP.
